panels.description: Zone with the largest demand, which feeds the boiler PID. Demand = target − room, in K. POSITIVE = the zone is below target and wants heat; negative = above target. Zones in off mode use the 16 °C off target.
panels.title: Leader / demand (+ wants heat)

targets.expr: count(max by (entity) (heating_entity_dependency) == 1 unless on(entity) (max by (entity) (homeassistant_entity_available) == 1)) or vector(0)

panels.description: PID terms are sign-inverted: NEGATIVE = MORE heat. I near +3 holds output near 0, near −3 pushes it to full. The node stops integrating when |P + I| reaches 3. Orange beyond ±2.5, red at ±3.
panels.title: PID integral (− = more heat)

panels.description: Orange = this zone had the largest demand. Demand = target − room, in K. POSITIVE = the zone is below target and wants heat; negative = above target. Zones in off mode use the 16 °C off target. On an exact tie every tied zone shows as leader; node-red picks the first in its zone order.
panels.title: Leader zone (largest demand, feeds the boiler PID)

panels.description: Of the minutes the boiler PID asked for heat (flow command above the 10 °C idle value), the share each zone was the leader. Tied minutes are split evenly between the tied zones, so the bars sum to 100. The backup 16 °C floor is excluded; over 7 days to 05 Nov it never led while the PID asked for heat.

targets.expr: sum by (zone) (sum_over_time((((max by (zone) (heating_flags{flag="is_leader"}) == 1) unless on(zone) {zone="backup"}) and on() (max(pid_component{component="payload"}) > 10))[$__range:1m])) / on() group_left() sum_over_time(((max(pid_component{component="payload"}) > 10) * 0 + 1)[$__range:1m]) * 100

panels.title: Leader share of heating time (selected range)

panels.description: Values are the PID node's internal terms, which are sign-inverted: NEGATIVE = MORE heat. P = room − target (negative when the room is cold). Output = 0.5 − (P + I) / pb, pb = 6, clamped to 0..1: P+I = 0 gives 0.5, P+I = −3 gives full output, P+I = +3 gives zero. The node integrates only while |P + I| < 3 (pb/2); at the dashed lines it stops. Dashed white line is P+I, the total that sets the output. Background bands are output levels in steps of 1.5: dark red below −3 (saturated, 75 °C), red −3..−1.5 (75..61 °C), orange −1.5..0 (61..47.5 °C), yellow 0..1.5 (47.5..34 °C), pale green 1.5..3 (34..20 °C), grey above +3 (output 0, 10 °C = no heat needed). 0 is only the 0.5 midpoint, not a switch. Solid lines are the two terms; all share one axis.
panels.title: Boiler PID: negative = more heat, frozen outside ±3

targets.expr: max by (entity) (homeassistant_climate_target_temperature_celsius{entity="climate.${zone}_thermostat"}) and on(entity) max by (entity) (homeassistant_climate_mode{entity="climate.${zone}_thermostat", mode="heat"}) == 1

panels.description: Demand = target − room, in K. POSITIVE = the zone is below target and wants heat; negative = above target. Zones in off mode use the 16 °C off target.
panels.title: Demand per zone (target − room): red band + wants heat, blue band − above target

panels.description: Controller intent every evaluation (at most every 2 min per zone), before rounding and before the 1 K write dedupe. push = 2·(error with 0.2 K deadband) + integral, where error = target − room. Positive: the TRV is told to aim above the zone target, so it opens more than it would on its own. Negative: told to aim below, so it closes earlier. Zones in off mode are not shown (command 16 °C). Exported since 2026-11-05 14:38 UTC.

targets.expr: max by (zone) (heating_flags{flag="push"}) and on(zone) (max by (zone) (label_replace(homeassistant_climate_mode{entity=~"climate.(workshop|livingroom|bedroom|nursery|drawing_room)_thermostat", mode="heat"}, "zone", "$1", "entity", "climate\\.(?:trv_)?(workshop|livingroom|bedroom|nursery|drawing_room)(?:_thermostat)?")) == 1)

panels.title: TRV push = command − target (K): red + opening the valve harder, blue − holding it back

panels.description: Setpoint writes the controller sent to each TRV in the trailing 24 h, including re-sends of the same value after a TRV reverted. Each write wakes a battery TRV. Counter heating_trv_writes, since 2026-11-05 14:38 UTC; resets on deploy are handled by increase().
panels.title: TRV writes per day (battery cost)

panels.description: hvac_action from the TRV: 'heating' = the TRV's own loop has its valve open (any amount). livingroom and drawing_room are Danfoss LC-13 on Z-Wave, which report no valve state at all.

targets.expr: max by (zone) (label_replace(homeassistant_climate_action{entity=~"climate.trv_.*", action="heating"}, "zone", "$1", "entity", "climate\\.(?:trv_)?(workshop|livingroom|bedroom|nursery|drawing_room)(?:_thermostat)?")) or label_replace(vector(-1), "zone", "livingroom", "", "") or label_replace(vector(-1), "zone", "drawing_room", "", "")

panels.title: Valve state reported by the TRV itself

targets.expr: max by (entity) (homeassistant_entity_available) and on(entity) max by (entity) (heating_entity_dependency)

panels.description: NOT valve position. How far the controller could still raise the TRV setpoint command, in kelvin (K, 1 K = 1 °C difference). Headroom = ceiling − current command, ceiling = min(30 °C, target + 2·max(0, target − room) + 5). The +5 is trv_integral_clamp, which is the limit that binds in practice (bedroom 01 Nov). Near 0 the controller cannot push that TRV further; whether the valve is open is in 'TRV valve activity'.
panels.title: Controller headroom on TRV command (K, not valve position)
